sections.h2: Which way should I sell a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
Gastonia owners can hire an agent, look for a buyer unaided, or take a cash offer on the house unrepaired. Repairs, timing and the discount you will accept for speed decide it.

  • Agent: widest exposure, with prep work, showings and a fee.
  • Unaided: no fee, but the contract work is yours.
  • Cash: your schedule and no repair list, usually at a lower number.

Many Gastonia houses date from the mill era, so cash offers often come up for homes carrying deferred work.

Gastonia began as a railroad depot in 1873, incorporated in 1877 and grew around its textile mills. It is the largest of Gaston County's 15 municipalities, with more than 72,000 residents on about 51.99 square miles.

That mill history left a mix of housing ages. Houses built around the textile era tend to have older wiring, plumbing and foundations, which is worth an inspection when you set the asking figure.

sections.h2: How Gaston County values a Gastonia house
sections.html:
The Gaston County tax office values every parcel, and the commissioners voted in 2025 to adopt a four-year reappraisal cycle. State law requires one at least every eight years, so Gaston now reappraises twice as often. Call the Gaston County Tax Office for your current assessed value and the date of the next reappraisal.

The county's formula is tax value divided by 100, times the rate. The county and the cities publish a revenue-neutral rate in the budget cycle, and a higher value may or may not mean a higher bill.

Bills are due September 1, and interest starts January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

If a bill is open when you sell, have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Where a Gastonia sale is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Gaston County register of deeds, and the closing attorney normally handles the filing and the fees on your settlement statement. Ask for that statement in writing before the closing date.

The county seat moved from Dallas to Gastonia after a 1906 referendum. Today the register of deeds, the clerk's office and the tax office all serve owners from the Gastonia area, so one trip often covers several steps. The courthouse stands at North Marietta Street and Long Avenue. Court filings tied to a sale, such as an estate matter, go there, so plan a trip or ask your attorney to file for you.

sections.h2: Tax relief at 65 or with a disability
sections.html:
The state allows one of three relief programs, filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes half the appraised value or $25,000, whichever is greater, and the state form prints the 2026 income limit as $38,800.

A disabled veteran exclusion is a separate program. Ask the Gaston County assessor which one fits and what deadline applies to your parcel.

A small estate can be collected by affidavit instead of full administration, with a $20,000 personal property limit for an intestate estate under G.S. 28A-25-1. A house is real property, so ask an estate attorney or the county court clerk who may sign the deed before you accept any offer.

If the house is also behind on tax, line up the clerk's file, the tax balance and the deed history together. Having all three in hand before an offer arrives keeps a closing from stalling over a missing document.

Sort out three things before the first showing: the age of the major systems, the paperwork on the lot, and who has authority to sign. Textile-era houses are often sound but carry old wiring, plumbing and foundations, so an early inspection tells you what a buyer will find.

  • Hire an inspector, or at least a roofer and an electrician, to price the big items.
  • Pull the parcel record from Gaston County and check the square footage and bedroom count.
  • Find the deed, any survey and payoff statements for each loan or lien.
  • For an inherited house, confirm with the clerk or an attorney who can sign.

The county's reappraisal visits every property and compares similar sales, so a house with improvements that are not on record may be valued low, while one with errors in its listing may be valued high. If something looks wrong on your record, raise it with the tax office before it becomes a bill.

If the house is vacant, secure it and keep the grass cut, since neglected properties draw complaints. Buyers paying cash will often accept such a house unrepaired, which is why owners with a vacant mill-district house often compare that route with a repair-and-list plan.

sections.h2: How long a Gastonia sale takes
sections.html:
Ask each buyer for a closing date in writing, since the route drives the calendar. A listing runs through showings, an offer, an inspection period and the buyer's loan, and a repair request can restart talks. Cash deals can close sooner since nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal.

Your attorney handles the search for liens, the closing and the recording, and can tell you how soon the deed will be filed after funds clear.

sections.h2: Questions to put to a buyer
sections.html:
Put the same questions to every buyer and keep the answers in writing. That makes two offers easy to compare, even when one looks larger.

  • Is the price firm, and what could change it after an inspection?
  • Does the buyer need a loan, or is it a cash purchase with proof of funds?
  • Who pays for the title search, the attorney and the recording?
  • How many days will the buyer take to close?
  • Will the buyer take the house with the furniture and debris still in it?

Cash Home Buyers gives written answers on Gastonia houses, including inherited homes, rentals and vacant properties.

faqs.q: Is Gastonia the Gaston County seat?
How often does Gaston County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every four years, a cycle the commissioners adopted in 2025.

faqs.q: Where is a Gastonia deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Gaston County register of deeds, usually by the closing attorney.

faqs.q: I inherited a house in Gastonia. Can I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, once you hold legal authority to sign. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes a small estate affidavit, and the court clerk can say which route fits.
